name: ALERT_DESCRIPTION_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE
doc: Alert Descriptions from RFC 5246 and others. The IANA TLS Alert Registry contains this list and references to the RFCs where their meaning is defined.

name: ALERT_DESCRIPTION_INTERNAL_ERROR
doc: Alert Descriptions from RFC 5246 and others. The IANA TLS Alert Registry contains this list and references to the RFCs where their meaning is defined.

name: AlertDescription
doc: An enumeration.

name: CERT_NONE
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_mode. Except for PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT, it is the default mode. With client-side sockets, just about any cert is accepted. Validation errors, such as untrusted or expired cert, are ignored and do not abort the TLS/SSL handshake.

name: CERT_OPTIONAL
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_mode. In client mode, CERT_OPTIONAL has the same meaning as CERT_REQUIRED. It is recommended to use CERT_REQUIRED for client-side sockets instead.

name: CERT_REQUIRED
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_mode. In this mode, certificates are required from the other side of the socket connection; an SSLError will be raised if no certificate is provided, or if its validation fails. This mode is not sufficient to verify a certificate in client mode as it does not match hostnames. check_hostname must be enabled as well to verify the authenticity of a cert. PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT uses CERT_REQUIRED and enables check_hostname by default.

name: cert_time_to_seconds
doc:
Return the time in seconds since the Epoch, given the timestring
representing the "notBefore" or "notAfter" date from a certificate
in ``"%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %Z"`` strptime format (C locale).

"notBefore" or "notAfter" dates must use UTC (RFC 5280).

Month is one of: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
UTC should be specified as GMT (see ASN1_TIME_print())

changed.text: Interpret the input time as a time in UTC as specified by ‘GMT’ timezone in the input string. Local timezone was used previously. Return an integer (no fractions of a second in the input format)

name: CertificateError
doc: A certificate could not be verified.

changed.text: The exception is now an alias for SSLCertVerificationError.

name: CHANNEL_BINDING_TYPES
doc: List of supported TLS channel binding types. Strings in this list can be used as arguments to SSLSocket.get_channel_binding().

name: create_default_context
doc:
Create a SSLContext object with default settings.

NOTE: The protocol and settings may change anytime without prior
      deprecation. The values represent a fair balance between maximum
      compatibility and security.

changed.text: RC4 was dropped from the default cipher string.
ChaCha20/Poly1305 was added to the default cipher string. 3DES was dropped from the default cipher string.
Support for key logging to SSLKEYLOGFILE was added.
The context now uses PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT or PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER protocol instead of generic PROTOCOL_TLS.
The context now uses VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN and VERIFY_X509_STRICT in its default verify flags.

name: DER_cert_to_PEM_cert
doc:
Takes a certificate in binary DER format and returns the
PEM version of it as a string.

name: enum_certificates
doc: Retrieve certificates from Windows’ system cert store. store_name may be one of CA, ROOT or MY. Windows may provide additional cert stores, too.

name: enum_crls
doc: Retrieve CRLs from Windows’ system cert store. store_name may be one of CA, ROOT or MY. Windows may provide additional cert stores, too.

name: get_default_verify_paths
doc: Return paths to default cafile and capath.

name: get_server_certificate
doc:
Retrieve the certificate from the server at the specified address,
and return it as a PEM-encoded string.
If 'ca_certs' is specified, validate the server cert against it.
If 'ssl_version' is specified, use it in the connection attempt.
If 'timeout' is specified, use it in the connection attempt.

changed.text: This function is now IPv6-compatible.
The default ssl_version is changed from PROTOCOL_SSLv3 to PROTOCOL_TLS for maximum compatibility with modern servers.
The timeout parameter was added.

name: get_sigalgs
doc: Return a list of available TLS signature algorithm names used by servers to complete the TLS handshake or clients requesting certificate-based authentication. For example:

name: HAS_ALPN
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation TLS extension as described in RFC 7301.

name: HAS_ECDH
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the Elliptic Curve-based Diffie-Hellman key exchange. This should be true unless the feature was explicitly disabled by the distributor.

name: HAS_NEVER_CHECK_COMMON_NAME
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support not checking subject common name and SSLContext.hostname_checks_common_name is writeable.

name: HAS_NPN
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the Next Protocol Negotiation as described in the Application Layer Protocol Negotiation. When true, you can use the SSLContext.set_npn_protocols() method to advertise which protocols you want to support.

name: HAS_PHA
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for TLS-PHA.

name: HAS_PSK
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for TLS-PSK.

name: HAS_PSK_TLS13
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for External PSKs in TLS 1.3 as described in RFC 9258.

name: HAS_SNI
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the Server Name Indication extension (as defined in RFC 6066).

name: HAS_SSLv2
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the SSL 2.0 protocol.

name: HAS_SSLv3
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the SSL 3.0 protocol.

name: HAS_TLSv1
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the TLS 1.0 protocol.

name: HAS_TLSv1_1
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the TLS 1.1 protocol.

name: HAS_TLSv1_2
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the TLS 1.2 protocol.

name: HAS_TLSv1_3
doc: Whether the OpenSSL library has built-in support for the TLS 1.3 protocol.

name: MemoryBIO
doc: A memory buffer that can be used to pass data between Python and an SSL protocol instance.

name: eof
doc: Whether the memory BIO is at EOF.

name: pending
doc: The number of bytes pending in the memory BIO.

name: read
doc:
Read up to size bytes from the memory BIO.

If size is not specified, read the entire buffer.
If the return value is an empty bytes instance, this means either
EOF or that no data is available. Use the "eof" property to
distinguish between the two.

name: write
doc:
Writes the bytes b into the memory BIO.

Returns the number of bytes written.

name: write_eof
doc:
Write an EOF marker to the memory BIO.

When all data has been read, the "eof" property will be True.

name: OP_ALL
doc: Enables workarounds for various bugs present in other SSL implementations. This option is set by default. It does not necessarily set the same flags as OpenSSL’s SSL_OP_ALL constant.

name: OP_CIPHER_SERVER_PREFERENCE
doc: Use the server’s cipher ordering preference, rather than the client’s. This option has no effect on client sockets and SSLv2 server sockets.

name: OP_ENABLE_KTLS
doc: Enable the use of the kernel TLS. To benefit from the feature, OpenSSL must have been compiled with support for it, and the negotiated cipher suites and extensions must be supported by it (a list of supported ones may vary by platform and kernel version).

name: OP_ENABLE_MIDDLEBOX_COMPAT
doc: Send dummy Change Cipher Spec (CCS) messages in TLS 1.3 handshake to make a TLS 1.3 connection look more like a TLS 1.2 connection.

name: OP_IGNORE_UNEXPECTED_EOF
doc: Ignore unexpected shutdown of TLS connections.

name: OP_LEGACY_SERVER_CONNECT
doc: Allow legacy insecure renegotiation between OpenSSL and unpatched servers only.

name: OP_NO_COMPRESSION
doc: Disable compression on the SSL channel. This is useful if the application protocol supports its own compression scheme.

name: OP_NO_RENEGOTIATION
doc: Disable all renegotiation in TLSv1.2 and earlier. Do not send HelloRequest messages, and ignore renegotiation requests via ClientHello.

name: OP_NO_SSLv2
doc: Prevents an SSLv2 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing SSLv2 as the protocol version.

deprecated.text: SSLv2 is deprecated

name: OP_NO_SSLv3
doc: Prevents an SSLv3 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing SSLv3 as the protocol version.

deprecated.text: SSLv3 is deprecated

name: OP_NO_TICKET
doc: Prevent client side from requesting a session ticket.

name: OP_NO_TLSv1
doc: Prevents a TLSv1 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing TLSv1 as the protocol version.

deprecated.text: The option is deprecated since OpenSSL 1.1.0, use the new SSLContext.minimum_version and SSLContext.maximum_version instead.

name: OP_NO_TLSv1_1
doc: Prevents a TLSv1.1 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing TLSv1.1 as the protocol version. Available only with openssl version 1.0.1+.

deprecated.text: The option is deprecated since OpenSSL 1.1.0.

name: OP_NO_TLSv1_2
doc: Prevents a TLSv1.2 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing TLSv1.2 as the protocol version. Available only with openssl version 1.0.1+.

deprecated.text: The option is deprecated since OpenSSL 1.1.0.

name: OP_NO_TLSv1_3
doc: Prevents a TLSv1.3 connection. This option is only applicable in conjunction with PROTOCOL_TLS. It prevents the peers from choosing TLSv1.3 as the protocol version. TLS 1.3 is available with OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later. When Python has been compiled against an older version of OpenSSL, the flag defaults to 0.

deprecated.text: The option is deprecated since OpenSSL 1.1.0. It was added to 2.7.15 and 3.6.3 for backwards compatibility with OpenSSL 1.0.2.

name: OP_SINGLE_DH_USE
doc: Prevents reuse of the same DH key for distinct SSL sessions. This improves forward secrecy but requires more computational resources. This option only applies to server sockets.

name: OP_SINGLE_ECDH_USE
doc: Prevents reuse of the same ECDH key for distinct SSL sessions. This improves forward secrecy but requires more computational resources. This option only applies to server sockets.

name: OPENSSL_VERSION
doc: The version string of the OpenSSL library loaded by the interpreter:

name: OPENSSL_VERSION_INFO
doc: A tuple of five integers representing version information about the OpenSSL library:

name: OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER
doc: The raw version number of the OpenSSL library, as a single integer:

name: Options
doc: An enumeration.

name: PEM_cert_to_DER_cert
doc:
Takes a certificate in ASCII PEM format and returns the
DER-encoded version of it as a byte sequence

name: PROTOCOL_SSLv23
doc: Alias for PROTOCOL_TLS.

deprecated.text: Use PROTOCOL_TLS instead.

name: PROTOCOL_SSLv3
doc: Selects SSL version 3 as the channel encryption protocol.

deprecated.text: OpenSSL has deprecated all version specific protocols. Use the default protocol PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER or PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT with SSLContext.minimum_version and SSLContext.maximum_version instead.

name: PROTOCOL_TLS
doc: Selects the highest protocol version that both the client and server support. Despite the name, this option can select both “SSL” and “TLS” protocols.

deprecated.text: TLS clients and servers require different default settings for secure communication. The generic TLS protocol constant is deprecated in favor of PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT and PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER.

name: PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT
doc: Auto-negotiate the highest protocol version that both the client and server support, and configure the context client-side connections. The protocol enables CERT_REQUIRED and check_hostname by default.

name: PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER
doc: Auto-negotiate the highest protocol version that both the client and server support, and configure the context server-side connections.

name: PROTOCOL_TLSv1
doc: Selects TLS version 1.0 as the channel encryption protocol.

deprecated.text: OpenSSL has deprecated all version specific protocols.

name: PROTOCOL_TLSv1_1
doc: Selects TLS version 1.1 as the channel encryption protocol. Available only with openssl version 1.0.1+.

deprecated.text: OpenSSL has deprecated all version specific protocols.

name: PROTOCOL_TLSv1_2
doc: Selects TLS version 1.2 as the channel encryption protocol. Available only with openssl version 1.0.1+.

deprecated.text: OpenSSL has deprecated all version specific protocols.

name: CLIENT_AUTH
doc: Option for create_default_context() and SSLContext.load_default_certs(). This value indicates that the context may be used to authenticate web clients (therefore, it will be used to create server-side sockets).

name: SERVER_AUTH
doc: Option for create_default_context() and SSLContext.load_default_certs(). This value indicates that the context may be used to authenticate web servers (therefore, it will be used to create client-side sockets).

name: RAND_add
doc:
Mix string into the OpenSSL PRNG state.

entropy (a float) is a lower bound on the entropy contained in
string.  See RFC 4086.

changed.text: Writable bytes-like object is now accepted.

name: RAND_bytes
doc: Generate n cryptographically strong pseudo-random bytes.

name: RAND_status
doc:
Returns True if the OpenSSL PRNG has been seeded with enough data and False if not.

It is necessary to seed the PRNG with RAND_add() on some platforms
before using the ssl() function.

name: SSLCertVerificationError
doc: A certificate could not be verified.

name: verify_code
doc: A numeric error number that denotes the verification error.

name: verify_message
doc: A human readable string of the verification error.

name: SSLContext
doc:
An SSLContext holds various SSL-related configuration options and
data, such as certificates and possibly a private key.

changed.text: The context is created with secure default values. The options OP_NO_COMPRESSION, OP_CIPHER_SERVER_PREFERENCE, OP_SINGLE_DH_USE, OP_SINGLE_ECDH_USE, OP_NO_SSLv2, and OP_NO_SSLv3 (except for PROTOCOL_SSLv3) are set by default. The initial cipher suite list contains only HIGH ciphers, no NULL ciphers and no MD5 ciphers.

The default cipher suites now include only secure AES and ChaCha20 ciphers with forward secrecy and security level 2. RSA and DH keys with less than 2048 bits and ECC keys with less than 224 bits are prohibited. PROTOCOL_TLS, PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT, and PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER use TLS 1.2 as minimum TLS version.

deprecated.text: SSLContext without protocol argument is deprecated. The context class will either require PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT or PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER protocol in the future.

name: cert_store_stats
doc:
Returns quantities of loaded X.509 certificates.

X.509 certificates with a CA extension and certificate revocation
lists inside the context's cert store.

NOTE: Certificates in a capath directory aren't loaded unless they
have been used at least once.

name: check_hostname
doc: Whether to match the peer cert’s hostname in SSLSocket.do_handshake(). The context’s verify_mode must be set to CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED, and you must pass server_hostname to wrap_socket() in order to match the hostname. Enabling hostname checking automatically sets verify_mode from CERT_NONE to CERT_REQUIRED. It cannot be set back to CERT_NONE as long as hostname checking is enabled. The PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT protocol enables hostname checking by default. With other protocols, hostname checking must be enabled explicitly.

changed.text: verify_mode is now automatically changed to CERT_REQUIRED when hostname checking is enabled and verify_mode is CERT_NONE. Previously the same operation would have failed with a ValueError.

name: get_ca_certs
doc:
Returns a list of dicts with information of loaded CA certs.

If the optional argument is True, returns a DER-encoded copy of the
CA certificate.

NOTE: Certificates in a capath directory aren't loaded unless they
have been used at least once.

name: get_ciphers
doc: Get a list of enabled ciphers. The list is in order of cipher priority. See SSLContext.set_ciphers().

name: get_groups
doc: Get a list of groups implemented for key agreement, taking into account the current TLS minimum_version and maximum_version values. For example:

name: hostname_checks_common_name
doc: Whether check_hostname falls back to verify the cert’s subject common name in the absence of a subject alternative name extension (default: true).

changed.text: The flag had no effect with OpenSSL before version 1.1.1l. Python 3.8.9, 3.9.3, and 3.10 include workarounds for previous versions.

name: keylog_filename
doc: Write TLS keys to a keylog file, whenever key material is generated or received. The keylog file is designed for debugging purposes only. The file format is specified by NSS and used by many traffic analyzers such as Wireshark. The log file is opened in append-only mode. Writes are synchronized between threads, but not between processes.

name: load_cert_chain
doc: Load a private key and the corresponding certificate. The certfile string must be the path to a single file in PEM format containing the certificate as well as any number of CA certificates needed to establish the certificate’s authenticity. The keyfile string, if present, must point to a file containing the private key. Otherwise the private key will be taken from certfile as well. See the discussion of Certificates for more information on how the certificate is stored in the certfile.

changed.text: New optional argument password.

name: load_default_certs
doc: Load a set of default “certification authority” (CA) certificates from default locations. On Windows it loads CA certs from the CA and ROOT system stores. On all systems it calls SSLContext.set_default_verify_paths(). In the future the method may load CA certificates from other locations, too.

name: load_dh_params
doc: Load the key generation parameters for Diffie-Hellman (DH) key exchange. Using DH key exchange improves forward secrecy at the expense of computational resources (both on the server and on the client). The dhfile parameter should be the path to a file containing DH parameters in PEM format.

name: load_verify_locations
doc: Load a set of “certification authority” (CA) certificates used to validate other peers’ certificates when verify_mode is other than CERT_NONE. At least one of cafile or capath must be specified.

changed.text: New optional argument cadata

name: maximum_version
doc: A TLSVersion enum member representing the highest supported TLS version. The value defaults to TLSVersion.MAXIMUM_SUPPORTED. The attribute is read-only for protocols other than PROTOCOL_TLS, PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT, and PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER.

name: minimum_version
doc: Like SSLContext.maximum_version except it is the lowest supported version or TLSVersion.MINIMUM_SUPPORTED.

name: num_tickets
doc: Control the number of TLSv1.3 session tickets.

name: options
doc: An integer representing the set of SSL options enabled on this context. The default value is OP_ALL, but you can specify other options such as OP_NO_SSLv2 by ORing them together.

changed.text: SSLContext.options returns Options flags: >>> ssl.create_default_context().options <Options.OP_ALL|OP_NO_SSLv3|OP_NO_SSLv2|OP_NO_COMPRESSION: 2197947391>

deprecated.text: All OP_NO_SSL* and OP_NO_TLS* options have been deprecated since Python 3.7. Use SSLContext.minimum_version and SSLContext.maximum_version instead.

name: post_handshake_auth
doc: Enable TLS 1.3 post-handshake client authentication. Post-handshake auth is disabled by default and a server can only request a TLS client certificate during the initial handshake. When enabled, a server may request a TLS client certificate at any time after the handshake.

name: protocol
doc: The protocol version chosen when constructing the context. This attribute is read-only.

name: security_level
doc: The current security level.

name: session_stats
doc: Get statistics about the SSL sessions created or managed by this context. A dictionary is returned which maps the names of each piece of information to their numeric values. For example, here is the total number of hits and misses in the session cache since the context was created:

name: set_alpn_protocols
doc: Specify which protocols the socket should advertise during the SSL/TLS handshake. It should be a list of ASCII strings, like ['http/1.1', 'spdy/2'], ordered by preference. The selection of a protocol will happen during the handshake, and will play out according to RFC 7301. After a successful handshake, the SSLSocket.selected_alpn_protocol() method will return the agreed-upon protocol.

name: set_ciphers
doc: Set the allowed ciphers for sockets created with this context when connecting using TLS 1.2 and earlier. The ciphers argument should be a string in the OpenSSL cipher list format. To set allowed TLS 1.3 ciphers, use SSLContext.set_ciphersuites().

name: set_ciphersuites
doc: Set the allowed ciphers for sockets created with this context when connecting using TLS 1.3. The ciphersuites argument should be a colon-separate string of TLS 1.3 cipher names. If no cipher can be selected (because compile-time options or other configuration forbids use of all the specified ciphers), an SSLError will be raised.

name: set_client_sigalgs
doc: Set the signature algorithms allowed for certificate-based client authentication. It should be a string in the OpenSSL client sigalgs list format.

name: set_default_verify_paths
doc: Load a set of default “certification authority” (CA) certificates from a filesystem path defined when building the OpenSSL library. Unfortunately, there’s no easy way to know whether this method succeeds: no error is returned if no certificates are to be found. When the OpenSSL library is provided as part of the operating system, though, it is likely to be configured properly.

name: set_ecdh_curve
doc: Set the curve name for Elliptic Curve-based Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) key exchange. ECDH is significantly faster than regular DH while arguably as secure. The curve_name parameter should be a string describing a well-known elliptic curve, for example prime256v1 for a widely supported curve.

name: set_groups
doc: Set the groups allowed for key agreement for sockets created with this context. It should be a string in the OpenSSL group list format.

name: set_npn_protocols
doc: Specify which protocols the socket should advertise during the SSL/TLS handshake. It should be a list of strings, like ['http/1.1', 'spdy/2'], ordered by preference. The selection of a protocol will happen during the handshake, and will play out according to the Application Layer Protocol Negotiation. After a successful handshake, the SSLSocket.selected_npn_protocol() method will return the agreed-upon protocol.

deprecated.text: NPN has been superseded by ALPN

name: set_psk_client_callback
doc: Enables TLS-PSK (pre-shared key) authentication on a client-side connection.

name: set_psk_server_callback
doc: Enables TLS-PSK (pre-shared key) authentication on a server-side connection.

name: set_server_sigalgs
doc: Set the signature algorithms allowed for the server to complete the TLS handshake. It should be a string in the OpenSSL sigalgs list format.

name: set_servername_callback
doc: This is a legacy API retained for backwards compatibility. When possible, you should use sni_callback instead. The given server_name_callback is similar to sni_callback, except that when the server hostname is an IDN-encoded internationalized domain name, the server_name_callback receives a decoded U-label ("pythön.org").

name: sni_callback
doc:
Set a callback that will be called when a server name is provided by the SSL/TLS client in the SNI extension.

If the argument is None then the callback is disabled.  The method
is called with the SSLSocket, the server name as a string, and the
SSLContext object.

See RFC 6066 for details of the SNI extension.

changed.text: After the callback assigns a new SSLSocket.context, later ClientHello messages on the connection are dispatched to the new context’s sni_callback.

name: sslobject_class
doc:
This class implements an interface on top of a low-level SSL object as
implemented by OpenSSL. This object captures the state of an SSL connection
but does not provide any network IO itself. IO needs to be performed
through separate "BIO" objects which are OpenSSL's IO abstraction layer.

This class does not have a public constructor. Instances are returned by
``SSLContext.wrap_bio``. This class is typically used by framework authors
that want to implement asynchronous IO for SSL through memory buffers.

When compared to ``SSLSocket``, this object lacks the following features:

 * Any form of network IO, including methods such as ``recv`` and ``send``.
 * The ``do_handshake_on_connect`` and ``suppress_ragged_eofs`` machinery.

name: sslsocket_class
doc:
This class implements a subtype of socket.socket that wraps
the underlying OS socket in an SSL context when necessary, and
provides read and write methods over that channel.

name: verify_flags
doc: The flags for certificate verification operations. You can set flags like VERIFY_CRL_CHECK_LEAF by ORing them together. By default OpenSSL does neither require nor verify certificate revocation lists (CRLs).

changed.text: SSLContext.verify_flags returns VerifyFlags flags: >>> ssl.create_default_context().verify_flags <VerifyFlags.VERIFY_X509_TRUSTED_FIRST: 32768>

name: verify_mode
doc: Whether to try to verify other peers’ certificates and how to behave if verification fails. This attribute must be one of CERT_NONE, CERT_OPTIONAL or CERT_REQUIRED.

changed.text: SSLContext.verify_mode returns VerifyMode enum: >>> ssl.create_default_context().verify_mode <VerifyMode.CERT_REQUIRED: 2>

name: wrap_bio
doc: Wrap the BIO objects incoming and outgoing and return an instance of SSLContext.sslobject_class (default SSLObject). The SSL routines will read input data from the incoming BIO and write data to the outgoing BIO.

changed.text: session argument was added.
The method returns an instance of SSLContext.sslobject_class instead of hard-coded SSLObject.

The server_side, server_hostname and session parameters are now validated as SSLContext.wrap_socket() validates them. Previously a context with check_hostname enabled and no server_hostname was accepted, and verified the certificate chain but never the peer’s identity.

name: wrap_socket
signatures: SSLContext.wrap_socket(sock, server_side=False, do_handshake_on_connect=True, suppress_ragged_eofs=True, server_hostname=None, session=None)
doc: Wrap an existing Python socket sock and return an instance of SSLContext.sslsocket_class (default SSLSocket). The returned SSL socket is tied to the context, its settings and certificates. sock must be a SOCK_STREAM socket; other socket types are unsupported.

changed.text: Always allow a server_hostname to be passed, even if OpenSSL does not have SNI.
session argument was added.
The method returns an instance of SSLContext.sslsocket_class instead of hard-coded SSLSocket.

name: SSLEOFError
doc: SSL/TLS connection terminated abruptly.

name: SSLError
doc: An error occurred in the SSL implementation.

changed.text: SSLError used to be a subtype of socket.error.

name: library
doc: A string mnemonic designating the OpenSSL submodule in which the error occurred, such as SSL, PEM or X509. The range of possible values depends on the OpenSSL version.

name: reason
doc: A string mnemonic designating the reason this error occurred, for example CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. The range of possible values depends on the OpenSSL version.

name: SSLErrorNumber
doc: An enumeration.

name: SSLObject
doc:
This class implements an interface on top of a low-level SSL object as
implemented by OpenSSL. This object captures the state of an SSL connection
but does not provide any network IO itself. IO needs to be performed
through separate "BIO" objects which are OpenSSL's IO abstraction layer.

This class does not have a public constructor. Instances are returned by
``SSLContext.wrap_bio``. This class is typically used by framework authors
that want to implement asynchronous IO for SSL through memory buffers.

When compared to ``SSLSocket``, this object lacks the following features:

 * Any form of network IO, including methods such as ``recv`` and ``send``.
 * The ``do_handshake_on_connect`` and ``suppress_ragged_eofs`` machinery.

changed.text: SSLObject instances must be created with wrap_bio(). In earlier versions, it was possible to create instances directly. This was never documented or officially supported.

name: SSLSession
doc: Session object used by session.

name: has_ticket
doc: Does the session contain a ticket?

name: id
doc: Session ID.

name: ticket_lifetime_hint
doc: Ticket life time hint.

name: time
doc: Session creation time (seconds since epoch).

name: timeout
doc: Session timeout (delta in seconds).

name: SSLSocket
doc:
This class implements a subtype of socket.socket that wraps
the underlying OS socket in an SSL context when necessary, and
provides read and write methods over that channel.

changed.text: The sendfile() method was added.
The shutdown() does not reset the socket timeout each time bytes are received or sent. The socket timeout is now the maximum total duration of the shutdown.
SSLSocket instances must be created with wrap_socket(). In earlier versions, it was possible to create instances directly. This was never documented or officially supported.
Python now uses SSL_read_ex and SSL_write_ex internally. The functions support reading and writing of data larger than 2 GB. Writing zero-length data no longer fails with a protocol violation error.
Python now uses SSL_sendfile internally when possible. The function sends a file more efficiently because it performs TLS encryption in the kernel to avoid additional context switches.

deprecated.text: It is deprecated to create a SSLSocket instance directly, use SSLContext.wrap_socket() to wrap a socket.

name: cipher
doc:
Return the currently selected cipher as a 3-tuple ``(name,
ssl_version, secret_bits)``.

name: client_sigalg
doc: Return the selected client authentication signature algorithm.

name: compression
doc:
Return the current compression algorithm in use, or ``None`` if
compression was not negotiated or not supported by one of the peers.

name: context
doc: The SSLContext that is currently in use.

name: do_handshake
doc: Start the SSL/TLS handshake.

changed.text: The handshake method also performs match_hostname() when the check_hostname attribute of the socket’s context is true.
The socket timeout is no longer reset each time bytes are received or sent. The socket timeout is now the maximum total duration of the handshake.

Hostname or IP address is matched by OpenSSL during handshake. The function match_hostname() is no longer used. In case OpenSSL refuses a hostname or IP address, the handshake is aborted early and a TLS alert message is sent to the peer.

name: get_channel_binding
doc:
Get channel binding data for current connection.  Raise ValueError
if the requested `cb_type` is not supported.  Return bytes of the data
or None if the data is not available (e.g. before the handshake).

name: get_unverified_chain
doc:
Returns raw certificate chain provided by the other
end of the SSL channel as a list of DER-encoded bytes.

name: get_verified_chain
doc:
Returns verified certificate chain provided by the other
end of the SSL channel as a list of DER-encoded bytes.

If certificate verification was disabled method acts the same as
``SSLSocket.get_unverified_chain``.

name: getpeercert
doc:
Returns a formatted version of the data in the certificate provided
by the other end of the SSL channel.

Return None if no certificate was provided, {} if a certificate was
provided, but not validated.

changed.text: The returned dictionary includes additional items such as issuer and notBefore.
ValueError is raised when the handshake isn’t done. The returned dictionary includes additional X509v3 extension items such as crlDistributionPoints, caIssuers and OCSP URIs.
IPv6 address strings no longer have a trailing new line.

name: group
doc: Return the currently selected key agreement group name.

name: pending
doc: Return the number of bytes that can be read immediately.

name: read
doc:
Read up to LEN bytes and return them.
Return zero-length string on EOF.

changed.text: The socket timeout is no longer reset each time bytes are received or sent. The socket timeout is now the maximum total duration to read up to len bytes.

deprecated.text: Use recv() instead of read().

name: selected_alpn_protocol
doc:
Return the currently selected ALPN protocol as a string, or ``None``
if a next protocol was not negotiated or if ALPN is not supported by one
of the peers.

name: selected_npn_protocol
doc:
Return the currently selected NPN protocol as a string, or ``None``
if a next protocol was not negotiated or if NPN is not supported by one
of the peers.

deprecated.text: NPN has been superseded by ALPN

name: server_hostname
doc: Hostname of the server: str type, or None for server-side socket or if the hostname was not specified in the constructor.

changed.text: The attribute is now always ASCII text. When server_hostname is an internationalized domain name (IDN), this attribute now stores the A-label form ("xn--pythn-mua.org"), rather than the U-label form ("pythön.org").

name: server_side
doc: A boolean which is True for server-side sockets and False for client-side sockets.

name: server_sigalg
doc: Return the selected server handshake signature algorithm.

name: session
doc: The SSLSession for client socket.

name: session_reused
doc: Was the client session reused during handshake

name: shared_ciphers
doc:
Return a list of ciphers shared by the client during the handshake or
None if this is not a valid server connection.

name: unwrap
doc: Start the SSL shutdown handshake.

name: verify_client_post_handshake
doc: Requests post-handshake authentication (PHA) from a TLS 1.3 client. PHA can only be initiated for a TLS 1.3 connection from a server-side socket, after the initial TLS handshake and with PHA enabled on both sides, see SSLContext.post_handshake_auth.

name: version
doc:
Return a string identifying the protocol version used by the
current SSL channel.

name: write
doc:
Write DATA to the underlying SSL channel.  Returns
number of bytes of DATA actually transmitted.

changed.text: The socket timeout is no longer reset each time bytes are received or sent. The socket timeout is now the maximum total duration to write data.

deprecated.text: Use send() instead of write().

name: SSLSyscallError
doc: System error when attempting SSL operation.

name: SSLWantReadError
doc:
Non-blocking SSL socket needs to read more data
before the requested operation can be completed.

name: SSLWantWriteError
doc:
Non-blocking SSL socket needs to write more data
before the requested operation can be completed.

name: SSLZeroReturnError
doc: SSL/TLS session closed cleanly.

name: TLSVersion
doc: An enumeration.

name: MAXIMUM_SUPPORTED
doc: The minimum or maximum supported SSL or TLS version. These are magic constants. Their values don’t reflect the lowest and highest available TLS/SSL versions.

name: MINIMUM_SUPPORTED
doc: The minimum or maximum supported SSL or TLS version. These are magic constants. Their values don’t reflect the lowest and highest available TLS/SSL versions.

name: SSLv3
doc: SSL 3.0 to TLS 1.3.

name: TLSv1
doc: SSL 3.0 to TLS 1.3.

name: TLSv1_1
doc: SSL 3.0 to TLS 1.3.

name: TLSv1_2
doc: SSL 3.0 to TLS 1.3.

name: TLSv1_3
doc: SSL 3.0 to TLS 1.3.

deprecated.text: All TLSVersion members except TLSVersion.TLSv1_2 and TLSVersion.TLSv1_3 are deprecated.

name: VERIFY_ALLOW_PROXY_CERTS
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags to enables proxy certificate verification.

name: VERIFY_CRL_CHECK_CHAIN
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags. In this mode, CRLs of all certificates in the peer cert chain are checked.

name: VERIFY_CRL_CHECK_LEAF
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags. In this mode, only the peer cert is checked but none of the intermediate CA certificates. The mode requires a valid CRL that is signed by the peer cert’s issuer (its direct ancestor CA). If no proper CRL has been loaded with SSLContext.load_verify_locations, validation will fail.

name: VERIFY_DEFAULT
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags. In this mode, certificate revocation lists (CRLs) are not checked. By default OpenSSL does neither require nor verify CRLs.

name: VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags. It instructs OpenSSL to accept intermediate CAs in the trust store to be treated as trust-anchors, in the same way as the self-signed root CA certificates. This makes it possible to trust certificates issued by an intermediate CA without having to trust its ancestor root CA.

name: VERIFY_X509_STRICT
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags to disable workarounds for broken X.509 certificates.

name: VERIFY_X509_TRUSTED_FIRST
doc: Possible value for SSLContext.verify_flags. It instructs OpenSSL to prefer trusted certificates when building the trust chain to validate a certificate. This flag is enabled by default.

name: VerifyFlags
doc: An enumeration.

name: VerifyMode
doc: An enumeration.
